title: Command Injection in subprocess with shell=True
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x standard library on POSIX and Windows (shell resolution differs per OS)
security_mechanism: With shell=True the argument string is handed to /bin/sh -c (or COMSPEC on Windows), so shell metacharacters in input (';', '|', '&&', '$(...)', backquotes) terminate the intended command and start attacker-controlled ones. Even without shell=True, an attacker-supplied value that begins with '-' reaches the spawned program as an option (argument injection) unless the call is positional and guarded.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters, headers, filenames, or environment values that are interpolated or appended into a command string or argv element.

tracking_guards: Prefer the argv-list form (shell=False) with the dynamic value as one element and a fixed executable path; if interpolation into a shell string is unavoidable, verify shlex.quote (not ad-hoc escaping) is applied; check for strict allowlist validation (e.g. ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$) before the value enters the command.
not_candidate_when: The command string is entirely constant, the dynamic value is passed as a single argv element to a program that accepts no options, or the value is validated against a strict allowlist grammar that excludes all shell metacharacters before use.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
